title: THE ADVOCATES ACT, 1961
long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the legal practitioners and to provide for the constitution of Bar Councils and an All-India Bar.

sections.section_title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Advocates Act, 1961. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall, in relation to the territories other than those referred to in sub-section (4), come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act. (4) This Act shall, in relation to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint in this behalf, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.

sections.section_title: Definitions
sections.text: (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,― (a) "advocate" means an advocate entered in any roll under the provisions of this Act; (b) "appointed day", in relation to any provision of this Act, means the day on which that provision comes into force; (d) "Bar Council" means a Bar Council constituted under this Act; (e) "Bar Council of India" means the Bar Council constituted under section 4 for the territories to which this Act extends; (g) "High Court", except in sub-section (1) and sub-section (1A) of section 34 and in sections 42 and 43, does not include a court of the Judicial Commissioner, and, in relation to a State Bar Council, means,-- (i) in the case of a Bar Council constituted for a State or for a State and one or more Union territories, the High Court for the State; (ii) in the case of the Bar Council constituted for Delhi, the High Court of Delhi; (h) "law graduate" means a person who has obtained a bachelor's degree in law from any University established by law in India; (i) "legal practitioner" means an advocate or vakil of any High Court, a pleader, mukhtar or revenue agent; (j) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (k) "roll" means a roll of advocates prepared and maintained under this Act; (l) "State" does not include a Union territory; (m) "State Bar Council" means a Bar Council constituted under section 3; (n) "State roll" means a roll of advocates prepared and maintained by a State Bar Council under section 17. (2) Any reference in this Act to a law which is not in force in the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu, shall, in relation to that territory, be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, in force in that State or that territory, as the case may be.

sections.section_title: State Bar Councils
sections.text: (1) There shall be a Bar Council for each State as specified, to be known as the Bar Council of that State, and for certain groups of States and Union territories as specified, and for the Union territory of Delhi, to be known as the Bar Council of Delhi. (2) A State Bar Council shall consist of the Advocate-General(s) ex officio, and elected members from amongst advocates on the electoral roll of the State Bar Council, the number depending on the size of the electorate, elected by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with as nearly as possible one-half of such elected members being persons who have for at least ten years been advocates on a State roll. (3) There shall be a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman of each State Bar Council elected by the Council in such manner as may be prescribed. (3A) Every person holding office as Chairman or Vice-Chairman of any State Bar Council immediately before the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1977, ceased to hold office on such commencement, but continued to carry on duties until successors were elected. (4) An advocate shall be disqualified from voting at an election under sub-section (2) or from being chosen as, and from being, a member of a State Bar Council, unless he possesses such qualifications or satisfies such conditions as may be prescribed by the Bar Council of India, and an electoral roll shall be prepared and revised from time to time by each State Bar Council. (5) Nothing in the proviso to sub-section (2) affects the term of office of any member elected before the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1964, but every subsequent election shall be held in accordance with the rules made by the Bar Council of India. (6) Nothing in clause (b) of sub-section (2) affects the representation of elected members in any State Bar Council as constituted immediately before the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1973, until reconstitution.

sections.section_title: Bar Council of India
sections.text: (1) There shall be a Bar Council for the territories to which this Act extends, to be known as the Bar Council of India, consisting of the Attorney-General of India ex officio, the Solicitor-General of India ex officio, and one member elected by each State Bar Council from amongst its members. (1A) No person shall be eligible for being elected as a member of the Bar Council of India unless he possesses the qualifications specified in the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 3. (2) There shall be a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman of the Bar Council of India elected by the Council in such manner as may be prescribed. (2A) A person holding office as Chairman or Vice-Chairman of the Bar Council of India immediately before the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1977, ceased to hold office on such commencement, but continued to carry on duties until successors were elected. (3) The term of office of a member of the Bar Council of India elected by a State Bar Council shall, in the case of an ex officio member of the State Bar Council, be two years from the date of his election or till he ceases to be a member of the State Bar Council, whichever is earlier; and in any other case, be for the period for which he holds office as a member of the State Bar Council, provided every such member shall continue to hold office until his successor is elected.

sections.section_title: Bar Council to be body corporate
sections.text: Every Bar Council shall be a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire and hold property, both movable and immovable, and to contract, and may sue and be sued by the name by which it is known.

sections.section_title: Functions of State Bar Councils
sections.text: (1) The functions of a State Bar Council shall be to admit persons as advocates on its roll; to prepare and maintain such roll; to entertain and determine cases of misconduct against advocates on its roll; to safeguard the rights, privileges and interests of advocates on its roll; to promote the growth of Bar Associations for effective implementation of welfare schemes; to promote and support law reform; to conduct seminars and organise talks on legal topics and publish journals; to organise legal aid to the poor in the prescribed manner; to manage and invest the funds of the Bar Council; to provide for the election of its members; to visit and inspect Universities as directed; to perform all other functions conferred on it by or under this Act; and to do all other things necessary for discharging the aforesaid functions. (2) A State Bar Council may constitute one or more funds in the prescribed manner for giving financial assistance to organise welfare schemes for indigent, disabled or other advocates; giving legal aid or advice; and establishing law libraries. (3) A State Bar Council may receive any grants, donations, gifts or benefactions for the purposes specified in sub-section (2), credited to the appropriate fund.

sections.section_title: Functions of Bar Council of India
sections.text: (1) The functions of the Bar Council of India shall be to lay down standards of professional conduct and etiquette for advocates; to lay down the procedure to be followed by disciplinary committees; to safeguard the rights, privileges and interests of advocates; to promote and support law reform; to deal with matters referred to it by a State Bar Council; to exercise general supervision and control over State Bar Councils; to promote legal education and lay down standards in consultation with Universities and State Bar Councils; to recognise Universities whose law degree qualifies for enrolment and to inspect Universities; to conduct seminars and publish journals; to organise legal aid to the poor; to recognise foreign law qualifications on a reciprocal basis; to manage and invest Bar Council funds; to provide for election of its members; to perform all other functions conferred on it; and to do all things necessary for discharging the aforesaid functions. (2) The Bar Council of India may constitute one or more funds for giving financial assistance for welfare schemes, legal aid or advice, and establishing law libraries. (3) The Bar Council of India may receive grants, donations, gifts or benefactions for the purposes specified in sub-section (2).

sections.section_title: Membership in international bodies
sections.text: The Bar Council of India may become a member of international legal bodies such as the International Bar Association or the International Legal Aid Association, contribute sums to such bodies, and authorise expenditure on participation of its representatives in international legal conferences or seminars.

sections.section_title: Term of office of members of State Bar Council
sections.text: The term of office of an elected member of a State Bar Council (other than a member referred to in section 54) shall be five years from the date of publication of the result of his election, provided that where a State Bar Council fails to hold elections before expiry of the term, the Bar Council of India may, for recorded reasons, extend the term for a period not exceeding six months.

sections.section_title: Constitution of Special Committee in the absence of election
sections.text: (1) Where a State Bar Council fails to hold elections before expiry of its term or extended term, the Bar Council of India shall constitute a Special Committee consisting of the senior-most ex officio member as Chairman and two members nominated by the Bar Council of India from the electoral roll, to discharge the functions of the State Bar Council until it is reconstituted. (2) On constitution of the Special Committee, all properties, assets, rights, liabilities and pending proceedings of the State Bar Council vest in or transfer to the Special Committee. (3) The Special Committee shall hold elections within six months of its constitution, extendable by the Bar Council of India for recorded reasons.

sections.section_title: Disciplinary committees
sections.text: (1) A Bar Council shall constitute one or more disciplinary committees, each consisting of three persons, of whom two shall be elected by the Council from amongst its members and one shall be co-opted from amongst qualified advocates who are not members of the Council; the senior-most advocate among the members shall be the Chairman. (2) Any disciplinary committee constituted prior to the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1964 may dispose of pending proceedings as if the section had not been amended.

sections.section_title: Constitution of legal aid committees
sections.text: (1) A Bar Council may constitute one or more legal aid committees, each consisting of not less than five and not more than nine members, as may be prescribed. (2) The qualifications, method of selection and term of office of members of a legal aid committee shall be as prescribed.

sections.section_title: Constitution of committees other than disciplinary committees
sections.text: (1) A State Bar Council shall constitute an executive committee of five members and an enrolment committee of three members, elected by the Council from amongst its members. (2) The Bar Council of India shall constitute an executive committee of nine members elected from amongst its members, and a legal education committee of ten members, five elected and five co-opted. (3) A State Bar Council and the Bar Council of India may constitute such other committees from amongst its members as it deems necessary.

sections.section_title: Transaction of business by Bar Councils and committees thereof
sections.text: (1) The Bar Council of India shall meet at New Delhi or such other place as it may determine for recorded reasons. (2) A State Bar Council shall meet at its headquarters or such other place as it may determine for recorded reasons. (3) Committees other than disciplinary committees shall meet at the headquarters of the respective Bar Councils. (4) Every Bar Council and committee (except disciplinary committees) shall observe prescribed rules of procedure for transaction of business. (5) Disciplinary committees shall meet at such times and places and observe such prescribed rules of procedure as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Disqualification of members of Bar Council
sections.text: An elected member of a Bar Council shall be deemed to have vacated office if declared by the Council to have been absent without sufficient excuse from three consecutive meetings, or if his name is removed from the roll of advocates, or if otherwise disqualified under any rule made by the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Staff of Bar Council
sections.text: (1) Every Bar Council shall appoint a secretary and may appoint an accountant and other staff as it deems necessary. (2) The secretary and accountant, if any, shall possess prescribed qualifications.

sections.section_title: Accounts and audit
sections.text: (1) Every Bar Council shall maintain books of accounts in the prescribed form and manner. (2) Accounts shall be audited by auditors qualified under the Companies Act, 1956, at prescribed times and in the prescribed manner. (3) A State Bar Council shall, by 31st December following the end of each financial year, send a copy of its accounts and auditors' report to the Bar Council of India and publish the same in the Official Gazette. (4) The Bar Council of India shall, by the same deadline, send a copy of its accounts and auditors' report to the Central Government and publish the same in the Gazette of India.

sections.section_title: Vacancies in Bar Council and committees thereof not to invalidate action taken
sections.text: No act of a Bar Council or committee shall be questioned merely on the ground of a vacancy or defect in constitution.

sections.section_title: Election to Bar Councils not to be questioned on certain grounds
sections.text: No election shall be questioned merely on the ground that due notice was not given to any entitled voter, if notice of the date was published in the Official Gazette at least thirty days before.

sections.section_title: Power to make rules
sections.text: (1) A Bar Council may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Chapter. (2) Such rules may provide for the election of members by secret ballot including postal ballot, preparation and revision of electoral rolls, publication of results; the manner of election of Chairman and Vice-Chairman; resolution of election disputes; filling of casual vacancies; powers and duties of Chairman and Vice-Chairman; constitution of funds for financial assistance or legal aid; organisation of legal aid; summoning and holding of meetings and quorum; constitution and functions of committees; qualifications and conditions of service of staff; maintenance of accounts; appointment of auditors; and management and investment of funds. (3) No rules made by a State Bar Council under this section shall have effect unless approved by the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Senior and other advocates
sections.text: (1) There shall be two classes of advocates, namely, senior advocates and other advocates. (2) An advocate may, with his consent, be designated as senior advocate if the Supreme Court or a High Court considers him, by virtue of ability, standing at the Bar or special knowledge or experience in law, deserving of such distinction. (3) Senior advocates shall be subject to such restrictions in practice as the Bar Council of India may prescribe in the interests of the legal profession. (4) An advocate of the Supreme Court who was a senior advocate immediately before the appointed day shall be deemed a senior advocate, subject to an option to opt out before 31 December 1965.

sections.section_title: State Bar Councils to maintain roll of advocates
sections.text: (1) Every State Bar Council shall prepare and maintain a roll of advocates, entering the names and addresses of persons entered as advocates under the Indian Bar Councils Act, 1926 immediately before the appointed day (subject to expressing intention to practise), and persons admitted as advocates under this Act on or after the appointed day. (2) Each roll shall consist of two parts: senior advocates and other advocates. (3) Entries shall be in order of seniority, determined for pre-existing advocates by date of enrolment under the 1926 Act; for pre-appointed-day senior advocates of the Supreme Court, by principles specified by the Bar Council of India; for persons enrolled or designated senior on or after the appointed day, by date of such enrolment or designation; and for enrolled attorneys, by date of enrolment as attorney. (4) No person shall be enrolled as advocate on the roll of more than one State Bar Council.

sections.section_title: Transfer of name from one State roll to another
sections.text: (1) A person on a State Bar Council roll may apply to the Bar Council of India for transfer of his name to another State Bar Council's roll; the Bar Council of India shall direct the transfer without fee, unless the application is made by a person facing pending disciplinary proceedings or is otherwise not bona fide, in which case the Bar Council of India may reject it after giving an opportunity to be heard. (2) On transfer, the advocate retains the same seniority he held on the former roll.

sections.section_title: State Bar Councils to send copies of rolls of advocates to the Bar Council of India
sections.text: Every State Bar Council shall send the Bar Council of India an authenticated copy of its roll and communicate all subsequent alterations and additions.

sections.section_title: Special provision for enrolment of certain Supreme Court advocates
sections.text: (1) An advocate entitled as of right to practise in the Supreme Court immediately before the appointed day, and whose name is not on any State roll, may express intention within the prescribed time for entry in a State Bar Council roll, and the Bar Council of India shall direct entry without fee. (2) Entry shall be made in order of seniority per section 17(3). (3) If such an advocate fails to express intention in time, his name shall be entered in the roll of the State Bar Council of Delhi.

sections.section_title: Disputes regarding seniority
sections.text: (1) Where the date of seniority of two or more persons is the same, the senior in age shall be reckoned senior. (2) Any other dispute as to seniority shall be referred to the State Bar Council concerned for decision.

sections.section_title: Certificate of enrolment
sections.text: (1) A certificate of enrolment in the prescribed form shall be issued by the State Bar Council to every person entered on its roll. (2) Every enrolled person shall notify any change of permanent residence to the State Bar Council within ninety days.

sections.section_title: Right of pre-audience
sections.text: (1) The Attorney-General of India has pre-audience over all other advocates. (2) Subject to (1), the Solicitor-General of India has pre-audience over all other advocates. (3) Subject to (1) and (2), the Additional Solicitor-General of India has pre-audience over all other advocates. (3A) Subject to (1), (2) and (3), the second Additional Solicitor-General of India has pre-audience over all other advocates. (4) Subject to the foregoing, the Advocate-General of any State has pre-audience over all other advocates, with seniority among Advocates-General determined by their own seniority. (5) Subject as aforesaid, senior advocates have pre-audience over other advocates, and pre-audience inter se among senior advocates and among other advocates is determined by their respective seniority.

sections.section_title: Persons who may be admitted as advocates on a State roll
sections.text: (1) A person is qualified for admission as an advocate on a State roll if he is a citizen of India (subject to reciprocity for nationals of other countries), has completed 21 years of age, holds a qualifying law degree (obtained before 12 March 1967 from any Indian University; or before 15 August 1947 from a University in undivided India; or after 12 March 1967 after a recognised three-year or two-academic-year law course; or a recognised foreign law degree; or is a barrister called before 31 December 1976, or has passed the article clerk's examination for enrolment as an attorney of the Calcutta or Bombay High Court, or holds another recognised foreign law qualification), fulfils any other conditions specified by rules of the State Bar Council, and has paid the prescribed stamp duty and enrolment fee (concessional for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes). (2) Notwithstanding sub-section (1), a vakil or pleader who is a law graduate may be admitted if he applies within two years of the appointed day and fulfils clauses (a), (b), (e) and (f) of sub-section (1). (3) Notwithstanding sub-section (1), certain categories of persons — including those who for at least three years were vakils, pleaders or mukhtars, or were entitled to enrolment as advocates of a High Court, or were entitled otherwise than as advocates to practise law before 1 December 1961, or were advocates of a Burma High Court before 1 April 1937, or are entitled under Bar Council of India rules — may be admitted on application and fulfilment of clauses (a), (b), (e) and (f) of sub-section (1).

sections.section_title: Disqualification for enrolment
sections.text: (1) No person shall be admitted as an advocate on a State roll if convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude, convicted under the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, or dismissed or removed from State employment on a charge involving moral turpitude — save that the disqualification ceases two years after release, dismissal or removal. (2) This does not apply to a person dealt with under the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.

sections.section_title: Authority to whom applications for enrolment may be made
sections.text: An application for admission as an advocate shall be made in the prescribed form to the State Bar Council within whose jurisdiction the applicant proposes to practise.

sections.section_title: Disposal of applications for admission as an advocate
sections.text: (1) A State Bar Council shall refer every enrolment application to its enrolment committee, which shall dispose of it in the prescribed manner, subject to any direction of the State Bar Council; the Bar Council of India may remove a name entered by misrepresentation, fraud or undue influence after a hearing. (2) Where the enrolment committee proposes to refuse an application, it must refer it to the Bar Council of India for opinion with grounds. (3) The enrolment committee shall dispose of the application in conformity with the Bar Council of India's opinion. (4) Where an application is refused, the State Bar Council shall inform all other State Bar Councils of the refusal, stating name, address, qualifications and grounds.

sections.section_title: Power to remove names from roll
sections.text: A State Bar Council may remove from its roll the name of any advocate who is dead or who has requested removal.

sections.section_title: Application once refused not to be entertained by another Bar Council except in certain circumstances
sections.text: Where a State Bar Council has refused an application, no other State Bar Council shall entertain a fresh application from that person without the prior written consent of the refusing Bar Council and the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Power to make rules
sections.text: (1) A State Bar Council may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Chapter. (2) Such rules may provide for the time and form for expressing intention under section 20; the form of enrolment applications and their disposal by the enrolment committee; conditions for admission; and instalments for payment of enrolment fee. (3) No rules under this Chapter shall have effect unless approved by the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Advocates to be the only recognised class of persons entitled to practise law
sections.text: Subject to this Act and rules made thereunder, from the appointed day there shall be only one class of persons entitled to practise the profession of law, namely, advocates.

sections.section_title: Right of advocates to practise
sections.text: Subject to this Act, every advocate whose name is on the State roll is entitled as of right to practise throughout India in all courts including the Supreme Court, before any tribunal or person legally authorised to take evidence, and before any other authority or person before whom he is entitled to practise by or under law. 31. [Repealed.]―Omitted by the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1976 (w.e.f. 1-1-1977).

sections.section_title: Power of court to permit appearances in particular cases
sections.text: Notwithstanding this Chapter, any court, authority or person may permit a person not enrolled as an advocate to appear in a particular case.

sections.section_title: Advocates alone entitled to practise
sections.text: Except as otherwise provided by this Act or any other law, no person shall, on or after the appointed day, be entitled to practise in any court or before any authority or person unless enrolled as an advocate under this Act.

sections.section_title: Power of High Courts to make rules
sections.text: (1) The High Court may make rules for the conditions under which an advocate may practise in the High Court and courts subordinate to it. (1A) The High Court shall make rules for fixing and regulating fees payable as costs in respect of an adversary's advocate's fees in proceedings in the High Court and subordinate courts. (2) The High Court at Calcutta may make rules for holding Intermediate and Final examinations for articled clerks under section 58AG and connected matters.

sections.section_title: Punishment of advocates for misconduct
sections.text: (1) Where a State Bar Council has reason to believe an advocate on its roll is guilty of professional or other misconduct, it shall refer the case to its disciplinary committee. (1A) The State Bar Council may withdraw a pending proceeding and direct inquiry by another disciplinary committee. (2) The disciplinary committee shall fix a hearing date and notify the advocate and the Advocate-General. (3) After hearing the advocate and Advocate-General, the disciplinary committee may dismiss the complaint, reprimand the advocate, suspend him from practice for a period it deems fit, or remove his name from the State roll. (4) A suspended advocate is debarred from practising anywhere in India during suspension. (5) The Advocate-General notified under sub-section (2) may appear in person or through an advocate.

sections.section_title: Disciplinary powers of Bar Council of India
sections.text: (1) Where the Bar Council of India has reason to believe an advocate not on any State roll is guilty of professional or other misconduct, it shall refer the case to its disciplinary committee. (2) The disciplinary committee of the Bar Council of India may, of its own motion, on report of a State Bar Council, or on application of an interested person, withdraw for inquiry any pending disciplinary proceeding before a State Bar Council's disciplinary committee. (3) The Bar Council of India's disciplinary committee shall follow the procedure under section 35, with references to Advocate-General construed as references to the Attorney-General of India. (4) The Bar Council of India's disciplinary committee may make any order a State Bar Council's disciplinary committee could make; the State Bar Council concerned shall give effect to such orders.

sections.section_title: Changes in constitution of disciplinary committees
sections.text: Where a disciplinary committee ceases to exercise jurisdiction and is succeeded by another, the successor committee may continue the proceedings from the stage left by its predecessor.

sections.section_title: Disposal of disciplinary proceedings
sections.text: (1) A State Bar Council's disciplinary committee shall dispose of a complaint within one year of receipt or initiation, failing which the proceeding stands transferred to the Bar Council of India for disposal as a withdrawn proceeding. (2) Proceedings pending on the commencement of the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1973 shall be disposed of within six months of commencement or one year from receipt/initiation, whichever is later, failing which they stand transferred to the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Appeal to the Bar Council of India
sections.text: (1) A person aggrieved by an order of a State Bar Council's disciplinary committee under section 35, or the Advocate-General of the State, may appeal to the Bar Council of India within sixty days of communication of the order. (2) The appeal shall be heard by the Bar Council of India's disciplinary committee, which may pass any order it deems fit (including varying the punishment), provided no order prejudicially affecting the aggrieved person is made without giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sections.section_title: Appeal to the Supreme Court
sections.text: Any person aggrieved by an order of the Bar Council of India's disciplinary committee under section 36 or 37, or the Attorney-General of India or Advocate-General of the State concerned, may appeal to the Supreme Court within sixty days, and the Supreme Court may pass any order it deems fit (including varying punishment), provided no order prejudicially affecting the aggrieved person is made without a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sections.section_title: Application of sections 5 and 12 of Limitation Act, 1963
sections.text: Sections 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963 apply, so far as may be, to appeals under sections 37 and 38.

sections.section_title: Stay of order
sections.text: (1) An appeal under section 37 or 38 does not operate as a stay, but the Bar Council of India's disciplinary committee or the Supreme Court may, for sufficient cause, stay the order on terms it deems fit. (2) Where a stay application is made before the appeal period expires, the disciplinary committee of the State Bar Council or of the Bar Council of India may, for sufficient cause, stay the order on terms it deems fit.

sections.section_title: Alteration in roll of advocates
sections.text: (1) Where an advocate is reprimanded or suspended, a record shall be entered against his name in the State roll; where an advocate is removed from practice, his name shall be struck off the State roll. (3) Where an advocate is suspended or removed, his certificate of enrolment under section 22 shall be recalled.

sections.section_title: Powers of disciplinary committee
sections.text: (1) A Bar Council's disciplinary committee has the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in summoning and examining witnesses on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, requisitioning public records, issuing commissions for examination of witnesses or documents, and any other prescribed matter — except that attendance of a presiding officer of a court requires prior High Court sanction, and attendance of a revenue court officer requires prior State Government sanction. (2) All proceedings before a disciplinary committee are deemed judicial proceedings under sections 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code, and the committee is deemed a civil court for purposes of sections 480, 482 and 485 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. (3) A disciplinary committee may send summons or process to any civil court for enforcement as if it were its own process. (4) A disciplinary committee may continue proceedings notwithstanding absence of the Chairman or a member on a fixed hearing date, except that final orders under section 35(3) require presence of the Chairman and all members. (5) Where no final order can be made for want of majority opinion, the case shall be laid before the Chairman (or Vice-Chairman) of the Bar Council concerned, whose opinion, after such hearing as he thinks fit, shall be the final order of the disciplinary committee.

sections.section_title: Powers of Bar Council of India and other committees
sections.text: The provisions of section 42 apply, so far as may be, to the Bar Council of India and to the enrolment, election, legal aid or other committees of a Bar Council as they apply to a disciplinary committee.

sections.section_title: Cost of proceedings before a disciplinary committee
sections.text: A disciplinary committee may order costs of proceedings, executable as an order of the Supreme Court (for the Bar Council of India) or the High Court (for a State Bar Council).

sections.section_title: Review of orders by disciplinary committee
sections.text: A disciplinary committee may, of its own motion or otherwise, review any order passed by it under this Chapter within sixty days of the order, provided a State Bar Council disciplinary committee's review order has no effect unless approved by the Bar Council of India.

sections.section_title: Penalty for persons illegally practising in courts and before other authorities
sections.text: Any person who practises in any court or before any authority or person where he is not entitled to practise under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment up to six months.

sections.section_title: Power to frame and publish lists of touts
sections.text: (1) High Courts, District Judges, Sessions Judges, District Magistrates and Revenue-officers (not below Collector rank) may frame, publish and amend lists of persons proved to be habitual touts. (2) No person's name shall be included until given an opportunity to show cause. (3) A higher authority may direct a subordinate court to inquire into alleged touts and report findings. (4) A copy of every such list shall be kept displayed in every relevant court. (5) The Court or Judge may exclude a listed person from the court precincts. (6) Acting as a tout while listed is punishable with imprisonment up to three months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both. (7) Defines "Judge", "subordinate Court", "revenue-office" and "tout" for purposes of this section. 46. [Repealed.]―Omitted by Act 70 of 1993 (w.e.f. 26-12-1993).

sections.section_title: Financial assistance to State Bar Council
sections.text: The Bar Council of India may give financial assistance by way of grant or otherwise to a State Bar Council in need of funds to perform its functions.

sections.section_title: Reciprocity
sections.text: (1) Where a notified country prevents Indian citizens from practising law or subjects them to unfair discrimination, subjects of that country shall not be entitled to practise law in India. (2) Subject to sub-section (1), the Bar Council of India may prescribe conditions for recognition of foreign law qualifications of non-citizens for enrolment purposes.

sections.section_title: Indemnity against legal proceedings
sections.text: No suit or legal proceeding lies against any Bar Council, committee, or member for any act done in good faith under this Act or rules made thereunder.

sections.section_title: Power of revision
sections.text: (1) The Bar Council of India may call for the record of any proceeding disposed of by a State Bar Council or committee from which no appeal lies, to satisfy itself of its legality or propriety, and pass such orders as it thinks fit. (2) No order prejudicially affecting a person shall be passed without giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

sections.section_title: Review
sections.text: The Bar Council of India or any committee (other than its disciplinary committee) may, of its own motion or otherwise, review any order passed by it under this Act within sixty days of the order.

sections.section_title: Power to give directions
sections.text: (1) The Bar Council of India may, in exercise of its general supervisory power, give necessary directions to a State Bar Council or its committee, which shall comply. (2) Where a State Bar Council is unable to perform its functions, the Bar Council of India may give directions to its ex officio member, which shall have effect notwithstanding the State Bar Council's rules.

sections.section_title: General power of the Bar Council of India to make rules
sections.text: (1) The Bar Council of India may make rules for discharging its functions, including conditions of voting eligibility and electoral rolls; qualifications and disqualifications for Bar Council membership; effect to the proviso to section 3(2); prevention of multiple enrolment; determination of seniority; minimum qualifications for admission to a law degree course; classes of persons entitled to enrolment; conditions of the right to practise; form for transfer applications; standards of professional conduct and etiquette; standards of legal education and University inspection; recognised foreign law qualifications; disciplinary committee procedure; restrictions on senior advocates' practice; form of dress/robes; fees; general principles for guidance of State Bar Councils and enforcement of directions; and any other prescribed matter — provided rules on professional conduct/etiquette or dress require Chief Justice of India approval, and rules on foreign qualifications require Central Government approval. (2) Rules on professional conduct/etiquette or dress in force immediately before the Advocates (Amendment) Act, 1973 continue in force until altered, repealed or amended.

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
sections.text: (1) The Central Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act, including matters otherwise within the rule-making power of the Bar Council of India or a State Bar Council. (2) Such rules may cover qualifications/disqualifications for Bar Council membership; manner of Bar Council of India's supervision and enforcement over State Bar Councils; classes entitled to enrolment; exemption from training/examination under section 24(1)(d); determination of seniority; disciplinary committee procedure; and other prescribed matters. (3) Rules may be made for all of India or for specific Bar Councils. (4) Where a Central Government rule is repugnant to a Bar Council rule, the Central Government rule prevails to the extent of repugnancy. (5) Every rule shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament for thirty days, subject to modification or annulment by Parliament, without prejudice to things already done.

sections.section_title: Repeal of certain enactments
sections.text: (1)-(6) Sets out, in stages tied to the coming into force of different Chapters, the repeal of specified provisions of the Indian Bar Councils Act, 1926, the Legal Practitioners Act, 1879, the Bombay Pleaders Act, 1920, the Supreme Court Advocates (Practice in High Courts) Act, 1951, relevant Letters Patent provisions, and the enactments specified in the Schedule, together with a special provision repealing sections 1, 3 and 36 of the Legal Practitioners Act, 1879 upon commencement of section 45A of this Act.

sections.section_title: Rule of construction
sections.text: From the appointed day, references in any enactment to an advocate enrolled by a High Court shall be construed as references to an advocate enrolled under this Act.

sections.section_title: Saving
sections.text: Nothing in this Act affects the Supreme Court's power under article 145 of the Constitution to make rules on the conditions for a senior advocate to practise in that Court, or to determine who may act or plead there.

sections.section_title: Elections to first State Bar Council
sections.text: The elected members of a State Bar Council constituted for the first time shall be elected by and from advocates, vakils, pleaders and attorneys entitled to practise in the High Court and ordinarily practising within the relevant territory.

sections.section_title: Term of office of members of first State Bar Councils
sections.text: The term of office of elected members of a first-constituted State Bar Council is two years from its first meeting, continuing until reconstitution.

sections.section_title: Rights of certain existing legal practitioners not affected
sections.text: Pleaders, vakils, mukhtars and revenue agents practising immediately before Chapter IV comes into force, who do not elect to be or are not qualified to be enrolled as advocates, continue to enjoy the same practice rights and remain subject to the same disciplinary jurisdiction as before, notwithstanding the repeal of the relevant earlier laws.

sections.section_title: Dissolution of existing Bar Councils
sections.text: (1) On constitution of a new State Bar Council (other than Delhi), all properties, assets, rights, liabilities and pending proceedings of the corresponding earlier Bar Council vest in or transfer to the new Bar Council. (2) Defines "corresponding Bar Council".

sections.section_title: Power to make rules pending the constitution of a Bar Council
sections.text: Until a Bar Council is constituted, its rule-making power is exercised by the Supreme Court (for the Bar Council of India) or the High Court (for a State Bar Council).

sections.section_title: Special provisions during the transitional period
sections.text: (1) Where a State Bar Council is not yet constituted or unable to function, the High Court performs its functions relating to admission and enrolment of advocates. (2) Until Chapter IV is in force, enrolment may proceed without approved rules, with enrolled persons entitled to rights under section 14 of the Indian Bar Councils Act, 1926. (3) Persons who were advocates before 1 December 1961, or enrolled under this Act, are entitled to practise in the Supreme Court until Chapter IV comes into force, subject to Supreme Court rules. (4) Certificates issued or renewed to legal practitioners under repealed laws during the transition period are deemed validly issued or renewed.

sections.section_title: Special provisions with respect to certain advocates
sections.text: (1)-(4) Deem certain categories of advocates (in Allahabad/Oudh, Hyderabad, Gujarat/Bombay, and Union territory Judicial Commissioners' courts) whose names were not formally entered on rolls due to non-payment of fees, or under prior territorial reorganisations, to have been validly enrolled, entitling them to apply for admission on the relevant State roll.

sections.section_title: Special provisions in relation to the Union territory of Pondicherry
sections.text: (1) Persons entitled to practise law in Pondicherry immediately before Chapter III came into force there are deemed enrolled advocates for the purposes of section 17(1)(a) and may apply for admission on the Pondicherry State roll. (2) Persons practising in Pondicherry before Chapter IV came into force there, who do not elect or qualify for enrolment, continue to enjoy prior practice rights and disciplinary jurisdiction.

sections.section_title: Special provisions with respect to certain persons enrolled by Mysore State Bar Council
sections.text: Persons admitted as advocates by the Mysore State Bar Council between 28 February 1963 and 31 March 1964 on the basis of a pleadership certificate are deemed validly admitted, with seniority reckoned from 16 May 1964, subject to provisos on transfer to another State roll.

sections.section_title: Special provisions with respect to certain persons enrolled by Uttar Pradesh State Bar Council
sections.text: Persons enrolled by the High Court between 2 January 1962 and 25 May 1962 and subsequently admitted by the Uttar Pradesh State Bar Council are deemed validly admitted from the date of High Court enrolment.

sections.section_title: Special provisions with respect to certain persons migrating to India
sections.text: Persons migrating to India from pre-partition India who were pleaders, mukhtars or revenue agents may be admitted and enrolled as such under the relevant earlier law upon application and citizenship/other conditions, retaining the same practice rights and disciplinary jurisdiction as before repeal.

sections.section_title: Special provisions in relation to the Union territory of Goa, Daman and Diu
sections.text: (1) Persons entitled to practise law in Goa, Daman and Diu immediately before Chapter III came into force there are deemed enrolled advocates for section 17(1)(a) purposes and may apply for admission on the Maharashtra State roll (excluding non-citizens). (2) Persons practising there before Chapter IV came into force, who do not elect or qualify for enrolment, continue to enjoy prior practice rights and disciplinary jurisdiction. (3) Corresponding local law is repealed upon commencement of this Act or relevant part in that territory. 58AF. [Special provisions in relation to Jammu and Kashmir.]―Omitted by the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation (Adaptation of Central Laws) Order, 2020.

sections.section_title: Special provisions in relation to articled clerks
sections.text: Persons who, before 31 December 1976, commenced articled clerkship and passed the Preliminary examination for enrolment as a Calcutta High Court attorney, may be admitted as advocates on the State roll if they pass the Intermediate and/or Final examinations by 31 December 1980, apply for enrolment, and fulfil clauses (a), (b), (e) and (f) of section 24(1).

sections.section_title: Special provision relating to certain disciplinary proceedings
sections.text: (1) From 1 September 1963, disciplinary proceedings against an existing advocate of a High Court are disposed of by the corresponding State Bar Council as if he were enrolled on its roll. (2) Pending disciplinary proceedings under the Indian Bar Councils Act, 1926 stand transferred to the corresponding State Bar Council, subject to provisos on cases already referred to or remanded by the High Court. (3) Pending disciplinary proceedings against a pleader, vakil, mukhtar or attorney subsequently enrolled as an advocate stand transferred to the State Bar Council on whose roll he is enrolled. (4) Defines "existing advocate". (5) This section has effect notwithstanding anything else in the Act.

sections.section_title: Removal of difficulties
sections.text: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to this Act, particularly in the transition from repealed enactments, the Central Government may by order make necessary provisions not inconsistent with the Act's purposes. (2) Such an order may have retrospective effect from a date not earlier than 1 December 1961.

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
sections.text: (1) Until a State Bar Council makes rules on a matter, approved by the Bar Council of India, the Central Government may make rules on that matter. (2) The Central Government, after consulting the Bar Council of India, may make such rules for any or all State Bar Councils by notification, which have effect notwithstanding anything in this Act. (3) Where Central Government rules and later State Bar Council rules (approved by the Bar Council of India) cover the same matter, the Central Government may notify that its rules cease to apply to that Bar Council from a specified date, without affecting things already done.
